Hi there service team,
The kennel attendant asked me to write about crate labels and the related handling notes for our Companion Animal Travel Desk workflow. Please make sure every label is legible, firmly attached, and matched to the booking record before the animal is accepted for travel. The welfare coordinator should review any comfort notes first, and the cabin team must confirm that the crate is secure, clean, and suitable for the journey.

When a transfer issue arises, follow the usual internal steps and place <<FACT F106>> in the escalation record without delay. For arrival pickup, the release file must include <<FACT F089>> and the handoff should not proceed until the paperwork is complete. If a claim is needed because of escape in transit, record <<FACT F120>> in the case notes and keep the customer file updated with the required reference material. Do not add assumptions to any of these records, and do not rely on memory when you update the file.

Please continue to check labels for live-animal indicators, destination details, and any handling warnings that may affect care in transit. If you notice a mismatch between the crate and the itinerary, correct it at once and advise the senior coordinator through the standard channel. Clear labeling protects the traveler, supports the cabin team, and helps Aurelia Skyways maintain consistent service.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
